text: Hassan Emilio Kabande Laija, born on 15 June 1999 in Zapopan, Jalisco, Mexico, is known professionally as Peso Pluma and is a Mexican singer and rapper recognized for his work in regional Mexican music, particularly corridos tumbados. He began playing guitar at age 15 by watching YouTube videos and started writing songs in a diary, initially facing ridicule from peers, which later became a form of therapy as he realized some of his emotions could be expressed through rhymes. Kabande is the son of Hassan Kabande and Rubí Laija; his father was born in Chiapas and is of Lebanese descent, with ancestors emigrating from Bethlehem in the early 1900s, and his mother’s relatives were residents of Badiraguato, Sinaloa. He grew up in Guadalajara and began collaborating with his cousin, Roberto "Tito" Laija Garcia, also known as Tito Double P, on live albums Disco en Vivo (2020) and Disco en Vivo, Vol. 2 (2020), released by the independent label El Cartel de los Ángeles. His debut studio album, Ah y Qué? (2020), featured twelve songs and collaborations with El Choforo, Lalo Reyes, and Jorge Morales El Jilguero, followed by the single "Relajado Voy" released on 7 October. He released "Mil Historias" with Hector Rubio on 13 November and "El Petter" with Decreto Real on 4 December before launching his second studio album, Efectos Secundarios (2021), preceded by "Con Dinero Baila el Perro" and "Lo Que Me Das." The single "Por Las Noches," a slowed-down sierreño track about an unintended breakup, was released on 11 June. "Todo Es Playa," a song about smoking marijuana, was his last release with El Cartel de los Ángeles before switching to Prajin Records under George Prajin, with the socio-political track "Spiral" released on 25 November. On 4 February 2022, he released "El Belicón" with Raúl Vega, a corrido anthem on local narcoculture, which went viral after its music video, directed by Barush, gained 10 million YouTube views in one month and received significant playlisting on Spotify. The song debuted at number 50 on Billboard Hot Latin Songs, peaking at number 46, becoming his first chart entry. In April 2022, he released the EP Sembrando (2022), which included "Signal" and five new songs, celebrating fans and the 420 holiday, and was credited with solidifying the rise of corridos tumbados. He collaborated with Tornillos and Polo Gonzales on "Sentosa" for Garena Free Fire. On 3 June, he released "30 Tiros," an acoustic corrido about his success story, with a music video directed by Barush. In August 2022, he released "Siempre Pendientes" with Luis R. Conriquez, which sparked controversy for glorifying drug lord Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán, including lyrics such as "JGL, traigo en las cachas orgullosamente" and "Cuido la plaza del señor Guzmán," and a music video directed by Cesar Acosta that received 2 million views in 24 hours before being removed due to public outrage. At the 8 Music Fest in Culiacán on 1 October, Kabande performed the song live as a replacement for Junior H, with an image of El Chapo projected during the performance, drawing backlash from audiences, organizers, the city council, and netizens, with El Colectivo de Mujeres Activas Sinaloenses, A.C. (CMAS AC) denouncing the act and calling for sanctions under Article 254 of the Penal Code for the State of Sinaloa, potentially resulting in up to two years in prison. The city council defended the performance, stating it supported artistic freedom despite disapproving of the image projection. Kabande denied any connections to the cartel, stating he is an artist who only sings what he writes. In a 2023 interview with Pepe Garza, he said the controversy was "nothing that cannot be fixed" and continued with his career. "Siempre Pendientes" peaked at number 27 in Hot Latin Songs, 155 on Global Excl. U.S., and number 174 on Global 200, becoming his first global hit on Billboard, and debuted at number 9 on Mexico Songs, charting for 20 weeks. He announced "El Gavilán" as his next single on 21 October, released with Tony Aguirre and as his second collaboration with Conriquez, which reached number 41 in Hot Latin Songs by year-end. On 18 November, he released "Ando Enfocado" with Jaziel Aviles and Codiciado. On 24 November, he co-released "AMG" with Natanael Cano and Gabito Ballesteros, a song named after the Mercedes-AMG G 63, which debuted at number 25 on Mexico Songs and later reached number 10, becoming his first top-ten hit. The song, which featured a music video of the trio partying in Mexican nightlife with brass player footage, also debuted at number 92 on the Billboard Hot 100 with 5.8 million US streams, marking his first entry on the chart. "AMG" ascended to number 10 on Hot Latin Songs and reached number one on Mexico Songs on 25 February. On 9 December, he released "Delivery" with Alemán, introducing an experimental shift with hip-hop beats. On 30 December, Fuerza Regida released their album Pa Que Hablen (2022), which included the track "Igualito a Mi Apá" with Kabande. "PRC," released on 20 January, was written about the daily life of a gangster and became his second Hot 100 hit on 18 February, with a music video starring Cano and Kabande as dealers gaining 10 million views in its first week. The song's opening line, "Me levanto, un baño y luego me pongo a forjar," went viral on TikTok, sparking a dance craze and controversy due to children re-enacting it. On 10 February, Kabande and Junior H released "El Azul," a war corrido about working for El Chapo using his 701 moniker, which was censored by Spotify in late April for referencing fentanyl. The song debuted at number 15 on Mexico Songs. On 27 February, Argentine rapper Nicki Nicole remixed "Por Las Noches," adding a female perspective and a new verse, which fueled a resurgence of the original version on the Hot 100 on 25 March. On 9 March, he released "El Hechizo" with Colombian producer Ovy on the Drums, receiving rave reviews and a music video directed by Cristian Aguilar. His concert in León, Guanajuato, was postponed from 11 March to 30 March due to logistical and permit issues, creating buzz over possible government control due to his activism on narcoculture and his appeal among adolescents in a poor region. On 16 March, "Ella Baila Sola," a sierreño track written by Eslabón Armado's lead vocalist Pedro Tovar about friends spotting a beautiful girl on the dance floor, was officially released after a TikTok premiere. On 17 March, Kabande released a remix of Yng Lvcas' "La Bebé," aiming for a sonic shift, which was released with a music video on 23 March. "Ella Baila Sola" debuted at number 1 on both Latin Streaming Songs and Mexico Songs for the week ending 1 April, becoming both artists' first number-one single on Mexico Songs, and also debuted at number 2 on Hot Latin Songs, number 10 on Streaming Songs, and number 26 on the Hot 100, with 16 million official US streams in its first week. The "La Bebé" remix charted at number 77 on the Hot 100 with 6.8 million streams. With "AMG," "PRC," and "Por Las Noches" charting alongside "Ella Baila Sola" and "La Bebé," Kabande achieved the most Hot 100 Spanish-language entries for any Mexican artist. In celebration of his success, he announced the Doble P Tour across 17 U.S. cities. On 30 March, Becky G recruited Kabande for the single "Chanel," the first single from her regional Mexican album Esquinas, co-written with Tito and Grammy-winning producer Edgar Barrera, narrating a failed relationship. Kabande received updated Latin certifications from the Recording Industry Association of America, with "El Belicón" certified 8× Platinum for 480,000 units sold.
